mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen three consecutive weeks (-37.7 to -35.0), indicating gradual return of commuting and associated incidental retail trips, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -37.7 to -35.0 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the 4 weeks following any 3-week consecutive WORKPLACES improvement of similar magnitude in held-out data.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed from +26.0 to -6.9 over three weeks, consistent with seasonal cooling reducing outdoor activity; this broader pullback in discretionary outings should also depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 20 points within a 3-week window
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from 26.0 to -6.9 between t-3w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks despite PARKS having fallen more than 20 points, rejecting the seasonal pullback linkage.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has steadily increased from 10.9 to 12.4, signaling growing time spent at home which substitutes for retail outings and should suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose monotonically from 10.9 to 12.4 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise, falsifying the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains deeply suppressed near -47, indicating persistent restrictions or commuter caution; while TRANSIT stays below -45 retail recovery should remain capped over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -45 for the current week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has stayed between -45.7 and -48.0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week even though TRANSIT remains below -45, rejecting the restriction-cap mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility rises while TRANSIT remains deeply depressed, it implies commuting recovery is driven by local/car-based trips rather than public transit, allowing nearby retail footfall to grow even without transit recovery, raising RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while TRANSIT stays below -45
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved while TRANSIT stayed flat near -47
regime_hint: partial reopening with low transit reliance
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over 2 weeks in periods where WORKPLACES increases but TRANSIT stays depressed, rejecting the decoupled-commute mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state restriction regime, stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility (around -15 to -17) reflects consistent essential-activity allowance, and under this regime RETAIL_REC should follow a modest mean-reverting recovery toward the recent four-week mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues declining over the next 4 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable, rejecting the steady-state recovery assumption.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC bottomed at -41.3 in t-1w and rebounded to -39.7 in t-0w; if this reversal persists for another week it signals renewed consumer momentum, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -41.3 to -39.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in the next week despite having risen for the prior two weeks, rejecting the momentum hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: As PARKS mobility falls and RESIDENTIAL mobility rises together, people shift leisure time indoors; this substitution effect may redirect some outdoor recreation spending toward indoor retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls while RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 26.0 to -6.9 while RESIDENTIAL rose from 10.9 to 12.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over 2 weeks in periods where PARKS falls and RESIDENTIAL rises simultaneously, rejecting the indoor-substitution mechanism.
